summary: A file system in a file through a loop device: FAT32 and KRFFS images on a disk's volume attached, mounted, written and read back, the writes found by the host's tools, the FAT32 image over a disk that sleeps its caller, an image on an ext2 volume, and one on a stick pulled from under it; the program is tests/cases/machine/loopdev_scenario.c

cases.behavior: a FAT32 image on a FAT32 volume is attached to a loop device, mounted, written and read back, every refusal holds, and the host finds the write inside the image file

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes the images it takes out of the copy after a pass

steps.does: boot the copy, run loopdevprobe vfat at the debug shell: an image of type vfat on the disk's FAT32 volume attached to loop0, mounted, read, written, unmounted, detached, attached again and read back, everything an attachment refuses, and Linux's loop ioctls, and end the machine with QMP's quit
take fat.img out of the copy's volume with mcopy and read its made.txt with mtype

assertions.checks: loopdevprobe's line says LOOPPROBE OK (vfat), never LOOPPROBE FAIL
the kernel says loop: loop0: /m/ for the image the probe attached on the volume
mcopy takes fat.img out of the volume the machine wrote, and mtype finds 'written through a loop device' in its made.txt

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the probe mounts the FAT32 volume of a disk of its own as /dev/disk0p1, and the host's mtools read the image the machine wrote there; tests/native/probes.cases runs loopdevprobe vfat natively on images in a tmpfs

cases.behavior: a KRFFS image on a FAT32 volume is attached to a loop device, mounted, written and read back, every refusal holds, a write through the device has synced the backing file when it returns, and the host's checker finds the image clean with the write in it

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes the images it takes out of the copy after a pass

steps.does: boot the copy, run loopdevprobe krffs at the debug shell: an image of type KRFFS on the disk's FAT32 volume attached to loop0, mounted, read, written, unmounted, detached, attached again and read back, everything an attachment refuses, and Linux's loop ioctls, and end the machine with QMP's quit
boot the copy again, run loopdevprobe durable, 128 writes to a file of the KRFFS image through loop0, each counted written and synced in /proc/loop, and end the machine with QMP's quit
take krffs.img out of the copy's volume with mcopy, check it with fsck.krffs --strict and read its /made.txt with readfile.krffs

assertions.checks: loopdevprobe's line says LOOPPROBE OK (krffs), never LOOPPROBE FAIL
the kernel says loop: loop0: /m/ for the image the probe attached on the volume
loopdevprobe's line says LOOPPROBE OK (durable), never LOOPPROBE FAIL: the device's syncs grow with its writes, at least one a write
mcopy takes krffs.img out of the volume the machine wrote, and fsck.krffs --strict exits 0 on it
readfile.krffs reads /made.txt out of the KRFFS image, and it says 'written through a loop device'

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the probe mounts the FAT32 volume of a disk of its own as /dev/disk0p1, and the host's tools read the image the machine wrote there; tests/native/probes.cases runs loopdevprobe krffs and durable natively on images in a tmpfs

cases.behavior: the FAT32 image's sequence over a disk that sleeps its caller, where the loop device must take no slot of the request pool, and the host finds the write inside the image file

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes the images it takes out of the copy after a pass

steps.does: boot the copy with rach2.blocklag=1, run loopdevprobe vfat at the debug shell, and end the machine with QMP's quit
take fat.img out of the copy's volume with mcopy and read its made.txt with mtype

assertions.checks: loopdevprobe's line says LOOPPROBE OK (vfat), never LOOPPROBE FAIL
mcopy takes fat.img out of the volume the machine wrote, and mtype finds 'written through a loop device' in its made.txt

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the disk sleeps its caller by rach2.blocklag on the kernel's command line; tests/native/probes.cases runs the same sequence, loopdevprobe vfat, natively without the lag

cases.behavior: an image on an ext2 volume is attached, mounted and written, and its second name, a hard link, is refused a device of its own

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the copy of the disk whose volume is ext2, run loopdevprobe ext2back at the debug shell, and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: loopdevprobe's line says LOOPPROBE OK (ext2back), never LOOPPROBE FAIL

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the probe mounts the ext2 volume of a disk of its own as /dev/disk0p1; tests/native/probes.cases runs loopdevprobe ext2back natively on the images in its workspace

cases.behavior: a USB stick pulled from under an image mounted on a loop device takes the device with it: the read in flight fails, both volumes unmount and the attachment lets go of its file

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot with the copy of the stick on qemu-xhci, run loopdevprobe pull at the debug shell, pull the stick with QMP's device_del once the probe says LOOPPROBE HOLDING, wait for its last line, and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: loopdevprobe's first line says LOOPPROBE HOLDING, reading through the image on the stick
QMP's device_del of the stick, st0, returns
loopdevprobe's line says LOOPPROBE OK (pull), never LOOPPROBE FAIL: the read failed, and both volumes unmounted
the kernel says loop: loop0: the device under its file has gone

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: it pulls a USB stick from the machine with QMP's device_del, which only QEMU's monitor does
